intended_uses_covered: Residential use subject to San Diego Municipal Code Section 141.0318
possible_placement_paths: Possible path: Movable Tiny House under San Diego Municipal Code Section 141.0318, if the premises, zone, structure, access, utilities, certification, fire/coastal constraints, and permit satisfy current city requirements.
clearly_allowed: Current San Diego Municipal Code Section 141.0318 regulates movable tiny houses as a limited use in zones marked L in the applicable use-regulation tables.
Current Section 141.0318 states that one movable tiny house may be permitted per premises in addition to ADUs and JADUs permitted under the separate ADU section.
Current Section 141.0318 includes specific DMV, siting, access, utility, certification, fire, coastal, design, and rental requirements.
clearly_not_allowed: Current Section 141.0318 states that a movable tiny house may not be used for a rental term of less than 30 consecutive days.
Current Section 141.0318 prohibits natural-gas connections to a movable tiny house.
unclear: Whether a specific parcel is eligible.
Whether the applicable zone and premises context permit the proposed movable tiny house.
Whether the proposed structure meets current DMV, certification, access, utility, fire, design, and siting standards.
How coastal, brush-management, habitat, fire-hazard, beach-impact-parking, or other site constraints apply.
Whether HOA, deed, lender, or insurance constraints apply.
local_office_to_contact: City of San Diego Development Services Department
City of San Diego Planning Department
source_quote_or_summary: The July 2026 San Diego Municipal Code places Movable Tiny Houses in a dedicated Section 141.0318 and treats them as a separately regulated limited use.
Section 141.0318 includes one-MTH-per-premises language in addition to ADUs/JADUs and lists zone, siting, access, utility, certification, fire, coastal, design, and rental conditions.
Information Bulletin 403 is dated October 2020. Use the current code where its allocation or other wording differs.
notes: High confidence for the existence and current text of the City Section 141.0318 path.
Do not present this as parcel approval. Surface it as a possible path requiring City Development Services verification.
Do not let the October 2020 bulletin override the current July 2026 code.

possible_placement_paths: Possible path: qualifying THOW as a primary or accessory dwelling in unincorporated San Diego County, if the parcel, density, structure, certification, fire, access, utilities, water, wastewater, inspections, and permits satisfy current County requirements.
clearly_allowed: County Planning & Development Services guidance says that, since September 4, 2025, the County considers a qualifying THOW a dwelling under the zoning ordinance.
The County Director's Determination says a qualifying THOW could be used as a primary or accessory dwelling under the current zoning ordinance.
The County requires a PDS permit, plans, third-party ANSI A119.5 certification, County construction requirements, and required inspections.
clearly_not_allowed: The County THOW policy does not change the allowed density or number of dwellings on a property.
County THOW requirements do not apply to park trailers in mobile-home or RV parks.

County environmental-health guidance says hauled water is not an approved potable-water source for new construction and composting toilets, holding tanks, and portable toilets are not approved wastewater disposal for THOWs.
unclear: Whether a specific property is in unincorporated County jurisdiction and is a legal lot.

local_office_to_contact: County of San Diego Planning & Development Services

source_quote_or_summary: County guidance says a qualifying THOW may be used as a primary or accessory dwelling when specific requirements are met.
The September 4, 2025 Director's Determination requires ANSI A119.5 certification and lists construction, fire, size, DMV, siting, utility, density, and zoning conditions.
The County THOW page requires a PDS permit, plans, certification, and inspections, with possible fire, legal-lot, septic, flood, grading, stormwater, electrical, and right-of-way review.
The County water and wastewater FAQ, revised March 30, 2026, recommends obtaining environmental-health approval and discussing the project with PDS before buying the THOW or land.
notes: High confidence for the existence and stated scope of the unincorporated County THOW path.
This record does not apply inside the City of San Diego, another incorporated city, Tribal land, or State or Federal land.
Do not present this as parcel, permit, water, wastewater, fire, or unit approval.

possible_placement_paths: Possible path: classify the tiny home type first, then verify local zoning/siting permission with the relevant Georgia city or county.
Possible path: modular or site-built dwelling route where Georgia building code requirements and local zoning/siting rules are satisfied.
Possible path: RV, THOW, or park model route only where local planning/zoning ordinances allow the intended siting and use.
clearly_allowed: The Georgia DCA fact sheet clearly separates tiny homes into RVs, manufactured/mobile homes, residential modular/industrialized buildings, and site-built dwellings.
The fact sheet says Georgia building codes generally apply to modular dwellings and site-built dwellings.
The fact sheet says RVs, park models, and THOWs are controlled by local planning and zoning ordinances for siting.
clearly_not_allowed: The fact sheet says RVs are intended for recreational or seasonal use only.
The fact sheet says THOWs in a mobile-ready state do not fall within the scope of Georgia state building codes.
unclear: Whether a specific Georgia city or county allows any given tiny home type or intended use.

source_quote_or_summary: Georgia DCA identifies four tiny home categories: RVs, manufactured/mobile homes, residential modular/industrialized buildings, and site-built dwellings.
DCA says local government zoning requirements vary widely and that prospective owners should obtain local permission to site the tiny home.
DCA states that tiny house construction appendix provisions must be locally adopted to be enforced.
DCA's construction-code documents page includes tiny house appendix materials and related state code documents.
notes: This is a state-source classification record, not a local placement record.
Use it to improve structure-type triage and to route Georgia users toward local zoning verification.
